parts.gloss: he who is able to practice

words.gloss: he who is able to practice

literal: Anger guarding, having learned, self-restraint he who is able to practice, his opportunity, Virtue will look for, by the path, having entered.
translation: Virtue itself will seek out the opportunity to enter the path of one who has learned to control his anger and practice self-restraint.
modern: கோபத்தைக் கட்டுப்படுத்தி, நல்லவற்றைக் கற்று, அடக்கத்தோடு வாழ்பவனுடைய நல்வாய்ப்பை, அறமானது அவனது வழியிலே நுழைந்து தேடிப் பார்க்கும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of self-restraint combined with anger management and learning. For a person who achieves this level of self-control, Virtue does not wait to be sought; rather, Virtue itself actively seeks out the right opportunity to enter their life's path and bless them. The word 'கதம்' means anger, and 'காத்து' means guarding or restraining it. 'செவ்வி' refers to the opportune moment or favorable time, showing that righteousness waits for the perfect moment to reward the self-controlled individual.
